## Why This Is Asked
Tests constant-time bit manipulation skills, branchless thinking, and understanding of 64-bit mask patterns.

## Key Concepts
- **Pairwise masks**: `0x5...` (alternating `0101`) isolates even bits; `0xA...` (alternating `1010`) isolates odd bits
- **Complementary shifts**: left-shift even bits by 1, right-shift odd bits by 1, then OR combines them
- **No branching**: all operations are O(1) and branch-free

- **128-bit generalization**: process four 32-bit chunks in parallel using a vectorized approach, or extend the mask pattern
- **Performance verification**: benchmark against naive loop-based implementations to confirm O(1) constant-time behavior

- Cryptography (byte-swap operations for AES, SHA)
- Network protocol implementations ( endianness conversion)
- Low-level systems programming where timing-constant operations matter

## Why This Is Asked
Tests precise bit-mmask construction under edge-case shifts; no loops/branches is a common constraint in low-level systems.

## Key Concepts
- Bit masks and ranges
- Safe shifts with variable width (1..32)
- No branching; single expression mask composition

## Code Example
```javascript
uint32_t clearRange32(uint32_t x, unsigned a, unsigned b) {
  unsigned w = b - a + 1; // width of range
  uint32_t ones = (~0u) >> (32 - w); // w ones in LSBs
  uint32_t mask = ~(ones << a); // zeros in [a,b], ones elsewhere
  return x & mask;
}
```

- What if inputs are signed; does behavior change in C/C++?
